topics.label: Water
facts: Water is a liquid that we drink every day.
Water covers most of the surface of Earth.
Rain is water that falls from clouds in the sky.
When water gets very cold it freezes and turns into ice.

questions.q: What do we drink when we are thirsty?
questions.fact: Water is the best drink when you are thirsty.

questions.q: What happens to water when it gets very cold?
questions.fact: Cold water freezes and becomes solid ice.
Rain falls from clouds when tiny water drops join together and get heavy.

questions.q: Which of these is made mostly of water?
questions.fact: Oceans, lakes, and rivers are all made of water.

topics.label: Food
facts: Food gives your body energy to play, learn, and grow.
Fruits and vegetables help keep your body healthy and strong.
Milk, cheese, and yoghurt help your bones and teeth grow strong.
Bread, rice, and pasta give your body lots of energy.

questions.q: What does food give your body?
questions.fact: Food gives your body the energy it needs to move and grow.

questions.q: Which of these helps keep you healthy?
questions.fact: Apples are full of vitamins that help keep you healthy.

questions.q: Which food helps your bones grow strong?
questions.fact: Milk has calcium, which helps build strong bones and teeth.
Bread is made from flour, and flour comes from wheat plants.

topics.label: Weather
facts: Weather is what the sky and air are like each day.
The Sun can make a day warm and bright.
Rain, snow, and wind are all kinds of weather.
Clouds are made of tiny drops of water floating in the sky.

questions.q: What do we call rain, sunshine, and wind?
questions.fact: Weather is what the sky and air are like each day.

questions.q: What should you wear on a rainy day?
questions.fact: A raincoat keeps you dry when it rains.

questions.q: What makes a day warm and bright?
questions.fact: Sunshine warms the Earth and makes the day bright.
Clouds are made of tiny drops of water floating in the air.

topics.label: Ice
facts: Ice is water that has frozen solid when it gets cold enough.
Water freezes into ice at 0 degrees Celsius, which is 32 degrees Fahrenheit.
Ice floats on water because it is slightly lighter than the same amount of liquid water.
When ice warms up, it melts and turns back into liquid water.

questions.fact: Ice is simply water that has frozen solid.

questions.q: At what temperature does water freeze?
Why does an ice cube float in a drink?
choices: Ice is slightly lighter than liquid water
Ice is full of air bubbles only
questions.fact: Ice is less dense than liquid water, so it floats.

questions.q: What happens when ice warms up?
choices: It turns into steam at once
questions.fact: Warm ice melts and becomes liquid water again.
